newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hogs early Monday sold at prices $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower than Friday, pressured by retreating packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Packer demand turned soft amid slipping operating margins, they said. Margins were eroded by sluggish pork demand and higher cash hog prices, sources said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower at $53.00 to $54.00 in the country and $54.50 to $56.50 at plants, sources there said.
Illinois hogs sold $1.00 lower at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $56.50 to $57.00 at plants.
Indiana hogs sold $1.00 lower at $53.00 to $54.50 in the country and $55.50 to $56.50 at plants. Ohio hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lowr at $52.00 to $52.50 in the country and $53.00 to $54.00 at plants.

Prices on hogs delivered to plants last week were up $2.50 to $3.00 from the previous week on light supplies, sources said. Light supplies were tied to increased fieldwork and a seasonal reduction in marketings, they said.
Runs Monday also were light, which surprised some buyers who expected to see more hogs after weekend rain curbed fieldwork and gave farmers time to sell hogs in parts of the eastern Corn Belt.
Rainfall reportedly was light, which allowed farmers to continue fieldwork early Monday, they said.
